text: Right-sizing compute — two symmetric mistakes, and how to avoid both.
An oversized capacity wastes budget on headroom nobody uses. An undersized one bursts and throttles constantly. Both come from sizing off a one-time guess instead of measured behavior.
Bursting once during an unusual spike is normal. Bursting every single day at the same hour means the baseline itself has actually outgrown the SKU.
Start with a reasonably conservative SKU. Watch utilization for a few weeks. Adjust based on real evidence, then repeat the observation period — this never fully settles, it just gets rechecked.
Evidence over guesswork, revisited over time. Next up: SLAs and SLOs — turning good enough into a real number.
